text:
linh: Heads up — quick-switch repro: sidebar quota control flashes another workspace's settings and then persists until a hard reload. Steps: 1) open ws-A, open sidebar quotas 2) rapidly switch to ws-B via workspace switcher 3) open sidebar -> shows ws-A quota numbers but the header says ws-B. Seen in prod and staging.

kevin: I can repro. Got Remaining quota: 12 but ws-B actually has 120 in the billing UI. Screenshot incoming.

linh: Console log snippet (sanitized):
```
GET /api/console/prefetch 200 OK
Response: { user: "u-742", prefetch: { quota: { remaining: 12 }, workspace_id: "ws-A" } }
```

anita: Looks like prefetch contains workspace_id but the client cache key is only user-scoped. Quick check: client caches as `prefetch:${userId}` so switching workspaces can read stale prefetch.

kevin: Confirmed. Code: `cache.set('prefetch:'+userId, resp)`. Should include workspace id in key or validate on read.

michael: Watch out: we prefetch a lot of heavy payloads. If we include workspace in key we'll increase cache cardinality and backend load. Another option: server should set `Vary: X-Workspace-Id` or return a smaller payload for cross-workspace prefetch.

linh: @michael good point. We could also keep a small lightweight prefetch for switch event (only quotas + flags) and lazily load heavy widgets after switch.

anita: API design debate: should prefetch be session-scoped or workspace-scoped? For multi-tenant isolation, server must never accidentally return a workspace's data keyed to a different workspace context. Server-side enforcement is safer.

kevin: For a fast mitigation I'll add a client guard: if resp.prefetch.workspace_id !== currentWorkspace then discard and force a fresh fetch. That avoids showing wrong numbers until we ship the cache-key change.

devx: :thumbsup: UX idea — show a subtle "loading workspace context" banner during quick switches so users understand the UI might be catching up instead of showing stale numbers.

michael: Telemetry note: our `console.prefetch.hit` metric is keyed by user only. If we key by `user+workspace` we can detect cross-workspace cache hits and measure how often this happens. Right now we silently undercount.

linh: Filed a quick ticket: https://go/rdw/CON-769 (placeholder). Owner: @kevin. Plan: 1) client guard (today) 2) change cache key to include workspace (this week) 3) server Vary header + reduce payload (next sprint).

kevin: I'll push a tiny client fix and add tests to ensure prefetch is rejected when workspace mismatch. PR in ~2h.

console-deploy-bot: Scheduled canary deploy: console-edge v1.42.3 -> canary cluster in 30m :rocket:

anita: Also can we add a prod log/alert when `prefetch.workspace_id` != request workspace id? That would help find other endpoints returning mis-scoped data.

michael: I'll add a telemetry counter and a rate-limited 5xx if we see mismatch > X/min to force investigation.

linh: Thanks all. Quick follow-ups: @kevin PR + tests, @michael telemetry changes, @anita server-side payload reduction. We'll patch canary and monitor metrics.
